criteria.title: Retained-evidence digest eligibility
criteria.relation_to_existing: Additive. Does not supersede Q6/Q17/Q18. Q18 binds fragment integrity and never grants safety; Q20 binds whether a retained observation may be reported green at all. Q17 still resolves claimed paths; Q20 additionally binds their current bytes.

proposed_row.criterion: A retained green observation is eligible only after a nonempty declared dependency map matches current regular non-symlink file digests, and a caller-declared required minimum is enforced so a record cannot silently narrow what is measured. The dependency digests must be captured with the original observation, not manufactured from current bytes at retention time, and the before/after dependency state must agree. Legacy/absent/empty dependencies, false or non-boolean matched, malformed record fields, missing/non-regular/symlink/hardlink/escaping/protected dependencies, and digest mismatches are ineligible and never reported green. Retention preserves each result's own measured_commit. This does not infer dependency completeness beyond the declared/required set, bind external runtimes or environment, authenticate execution, or prove the producer was re-run.
proposed_row.test: `python3 -B tools/souji-evidence-cache.py --selftest` and `python3 -B tests/fixtures/r14-evidence-cache.py --tool tools/souji-evidence-cache.py` must both exit 0 with the immutable expected finding-id/exit matrix; `python3 -B census/round-14/cache-demonstration.py` must show one unchanged record reusable and the same record stale after a one-byte dependency change, with the original measured_commit in both outputs and a source-derived red-before against the old matched-only branch. A changed dependency must be refused (exit 1, dependency-digest-mismatch), not retained green; the caller, not the gate, re-runs the producer. Do not use `--retry-failed` or copy any prior green.
proposed_row.lesson: corpus/lessons/round-14.md ## Mistakes R14-M1; corpus/lessons/round-13-verifier-spotcheck.md ## Routed findings, item 3 (prior spotcheck retention caveat); census/round-13/run-verification.py:48-54

lesson_grounding.pointer: corpus/lessons/round-13-verifier-spotcheck.md:132 (## Routed findings and review adjudication, item 3)
lesson_grounding.fact: The r13 runner's retained-green selection does not compare tool digests before retaining an old observation; per-result revisions must not be erased.

`run()` returns a shallow copy of the prior result for any name not in RETRY_NAMES; RETRY_NAMES contains only prior results with `matched` false. It sets measured_commit only via `.get(...)`, adds `retained_from`, and never reads or hashes a dependency. A prior green survives any dependency change.

Retained results `evidence-frozen`, `structure-selftest`, `historical-replay-wrong-bytes` and `historical-replay-candidate` name measured_commit 6ed10a7 while the record-level revision is 6f8ee0f. The r13 closure validated the unchanged bytes manually; the selector itself did not.
Passing checks are retained with their own measured commit; only failed checks are retried after corrections. Q20 makes that practice mechanically checkable rather than documentary.
A stale historical artifact retained a CERTIFIED claim; the round had to supersede it explicitly. Q20 prevents the same shape for retained green measurements.

Stale-green evidence retention can retain an old success after the measured tool changes; the fix is a digest-bound eligibility gate and a current-round consumer preserving the original measured revision.

failure_precondition.statement: A previously green result is retained by name alone. Eligibility is decided from the prior record's boolean `matched`, not from current bytes. The prior file may name a measured revision, but no code compares the recorded dependency digests (there are none) or the tool/fixture bytes. Therefore a changed tool, fixture, or input remains green indefinitely; `retained_from` records provenance, not eligibility.
failure_precondition.why_r13_did_not_catch_it: The r13 closure manually compared unchanged files and the sole parser delta. That is an external check, not an encoded selector rule.
failure_precondition.fix_boundary: The C1 gate makes eligibility re-derivable. In the working tree, the historical runner's retention branch now consults the gate (source inspection; not exercised by this seat), and the r14 runner (census/round-14/run-verification.py) avoids --retry-failed entirely. The baseline branch at a31642d remains the red-before. The gate alone does not prove observation-time capture or complete dependencies.
variants: Name-only retention (observed): a prior matched=true result is returned without any digest check (census/round-13/run-verification.py:48-54).

Digest laundering (procedural): a consumer could hash current bytes and write a fresh-looking record at retention time. The gate cannot distinguish that from observation-time capture; Q20 forbids it, and the demonstration must show the record was built before the changed byte.
Dependency narrowing (partially mitigated): a record with a smaller dependency set passes; --require lets the caller enforce a minimum, but only that minimum.

eligibility_rules: `matched` is exactly the JSON boolean true; false, absent, null, 0, 1 and "true" are ineligible.
`measured_commit` is a full 40-character lowercase hex revision and is echoed unchanged; it is never defaulted from HEAD, a top-level record, or a previous attempt.
`dependencies` is a nonempty object of relative POSIX paths to 64-character lowercase sha256 values. Legacy/absent and empty maps are ineligible.

Dependency digests are observation-time data: a consumer must not re-hash current bytes at retention time and write them into the record. The gate cannot detect a record manufactured after the fact; Q20 requires the record to carry a pre-existing map and requires before/after state agreement in the consumer demonstration.

Every dependency resolves under the declared root through non-symlink components to a regular, non-hardlinked file; absolute, `..`-escaping, symlink, hardlink, non-regular, protected-name, and too-large dependencies are ineligible.
Every current digest equals its declaration. A missing file or changed byte is stale (exit 1), never reusable.

A caller may pass `--require REL` as a minimum set; an undeclared required path is `dependency-undeclared` and ineligible. This raises the floor but does not prove completeness beyond the caller's list.
Level-2 findings dominate level-1 findings: a malformed record cannot be laundered into a mere stale verdict.

Eligibility is point-in-time and consistency-only: it never proves the command ran, that the recorded revision is true, that the dependency map was captured at observation time, or that the dependency list is complete.

criteria.title: Pre-access census boundary for the credential namespace
criteria.relation_to_existing: Additive to Q14 (operator-tooling runtime is report-only) and Q19 (bounds/special files). Q21 binds access order for the credential namespace; Q14/Q19 do not.

proposed_row.criterion: A census invocation must refuse before repository enumeration or any git, find, du, digest, or content read when the effective root (explicit or default), the --compare input, a repository .git/common-dir/alternates target, or a worktree/.scratch target overlaps the protected credential namespace. Overlap includes the store root, any ancestor or descendant, lexical . / .. aliases, and symlink aliases. Lexical component rejection runs first; filesystem-aware resolution is used only to catch aliases. Refusal is a stable named finding with exit 2 and emits no repo row; a normal out-of-boundary root keeps its legacy metadata output.
proposed_row.test: `python3 -B tests/fixtures/r14-census-boundary.py --tool <baseline-or-installed>`: synthetic HOME only; baseline a31642d must fail for the named boundary reason and the installed tool must pass; spies must observe no forbidden git/find/du/content read in direct, descendant, ancestor, root-symlink, compare-alias, gitdir-alias, and scratch-symlink cases; a safe normal root must remain exit 0 with its metadata row. A marker or exit code without access-order evidence is not proof.
proposed_row.lesson: corpus/lessons/round-14.md ## Mistakes R14-M3; corpus/lessons/round-13.md ## Mistakes R13-M7; PROVINCE.md ## Refuses (credentials are kagi's province); S040 (pure path computation vs filesystem-aware resolution)

lesson_grounding.fact: Arbitrary census input can point at the credential store or an ancestor and reach metadata/content readers; the baseline main/emit_census/emit_compare had no pre-access enforcement rule.
A guard that does not cover the class it claims is not a guard: optional locks were mistaken for a no-write guarantee; partial/promisor repositories had to be refused before enumeration.

An unscoped read-only regex over the lane returned lines from protected operator-sweep directories before the search was narrowed. The boundary was applied after access, not before. No credential store was touched.
Credentials, secrets, tokens and vault refs are kagi's province; souji cites paths/modes only and never reads secret content; credential-shaped content is NOT-SAFE.
